biomarkers.name: ER, PR, HER2
biomarkers.prevalence: ER/PR expression is less frequent than in non-IBC; HER2 overexpression/amplification is reported in ~30–40%; TNBC in ~20–30% (HER2-positive and TNBC enriched vs non-IBC)
biomarkers.clinical_use: Guides systemic therapy — trimodality therapy (neoadjuvant systemic therapy → mastectomy → RT) is standard

biomarkers.name: PD-L1 (in TNBC subset)
biomarkers.clinical_use: Pembrolizumab + chemotherapy in PD-L1-positive metastatic TNBC and in high-risk early-stage TNBC as part of neoadjuvant/adjuvant therapy

histomorphological_subtype.primary_pattern: Underlying invasive carcinoma (usually ductal NST) with dermal lymphatic invasion by tumour emboli — clinicopathologic diagnosis
variants: typically invasive ductal NST underlying; occasional lobular

tumor_microenvironment.immune_context: Paradoxical — 'inflammatory' clinical appearance is from lymphatic obstruction, not immune infiltrate; TIL variable per molecular subtype
tumor_microenvironment.stromal_features: Dermal lymphatic tumour emboli; peau d'orange appearance

cellular_states_and_lineage.cell_of_origin: Luminal or basal epithelium — clinicopathologic entity defined by dermal lymphovascular invasion, not a distinct cell of origin
cellular_states_and_lineage.developmental_lineage: Ectoderm — mammary epithelium is an ectodermal derivative
cellular_states_and_lineage.differentiation_state: Variable — can be any intrinsic subtype (luminal, HER2-positive, TNBC); enriched for high-grade tumours with EMT-associated features
cellular_states_and_lineage.lineage_plasticity: Dermal lymphovascular invasion is the defining feature — reflects a state of high invasiveness with lymphatic tropism; EMT-related signatures have been reported
